canonical.name: Asymptotic resource comparison packages eventual upper bounds and the usual polynomial-scale notions used by DTIME, DSPACE, and invariance claims
A computation bounded by T(n) steps with T(n) at least n has enough time to scan every input position once
A standard delimiter encoding of all work tapes on one tape preserves space up to a constant factor under single-tape simulation
A time-constructible bound lets one build a clocked simulator that halts after the permitted budget while preserving the simulated machine's answer inside that budget
Reasonable machine models preserve polynomial classes only up to quantitative overhead, not by matching exact step counts
Constructibility is load-bearing in clocking and hierarchy arguments because the simulator must compute and enforce its own resource budget
